answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one rule: admission costs a non-refundable stake a single human identity can post only once. Any extra identity must post the same collateral again, and it is slashed if caught. So N sock puppets cost N times the deposit while each earns one unit, and over a long horizon the attacker cannot recycle capital between waves. The attack loses money once the deposit exceeds expected earnings. That anchor makes cloning expensive, and verifiers read the stake ledger rather than guessing. A slashed clone is a saffron flag on the chain.
